headline: 3,431 passengers stranded as 10 Dhaka flights cancelled due to Riyadh airport closure
summary: Flight disruptions occur after Houthi attacks on Saudi aviation facilities, including King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and King Fahd International Airport in Dammam.
details: The closure of King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh following successive attacks has led to the cancellation of 10 flights from Dhaka, affecting 3,431 passengers, according to the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB).
Saudia and Riyadh Air cancelled three flights each, while Biman Bangladesh Airlines and US-Bangla Airlines cancelled two each.
The disruptions come amid escalating attacks on Saudi aviation facilities. A separate strike on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam also caused further flight cancellations and delays.
Yemen's Houthi group claimed responsibility for the attacks on the Riyadh and Dammam airports, as well as Saudi oil facilities.
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree warned that other Saudi airports and airspace remained potential targets, urging airlines and travellers to take the threat seriously.

The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) has recommended that airlines avoid two specified areas of Saudi airspace and exercise caution in the Jeddah Flight Information Region due to risks from missile and drone attacks.

International carriers like IndiGo have also faced cancellations on flights to Riyadh from Delhi and Hyderabad. Biman Bangladesh Airlines' Dhaka–Dammam flight was diverted to Doha before eventually landing in Dammam.
The disruptions have added uncertainty for Bangladeshi migrant workers and pilgrims, for whom Saudi Arabia is a major destination.

Over 3,400 passengers are stranded as 10 flights from Dhaka to Saudi Arabia are cancelled following airport attacks.

The closure of King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh following successive attacks has led to the cancellation of 10 flights from Dhaka, affecting 3,431 passengers, according to the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB).

Saudia and Riyadh Air cancelled three flights each, while Biman Bangladesh Airlines and US-Bangla Airlines cancelled two each.

The disruptions come amid escalating attacks on Saudi aviation facilities. A separate strike on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam also caused further flight cancellations and delays.

Yemen's Houthi group claimed responsibility for the attacks on the Riyadh and Dammam airports, as well as Saudi oil facilities.

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree warned that other Saudi airports and airspace remained potential targets, urging airlines and travellers to take the threat seriously.

The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) has recommended that airlines avoid two specified areas of Saudi airspace and exercise caution in the Jeddah Flight Information Region due to risks from missile and drone attacks.

International carriers like IndiGo have also faced cancellations on flights to Riyadh from Delhi and Hyderabad. Biman Bangladesh Airlines' Dhaka–Dammam flight was diverted to Doha before eventually landing in Dammam.

The disruptions have added uncertainty for Bangladeshi migrant workers and pilgrims, for whom Saudi Arabia is a major destination.
